subject: Runtime economics onboarding sync — batching, cache, quant & routing
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@brightgrid.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Runtime economics onboarding sync — batching, cache, quant & routing

Hi Aisha / BrightGrid EngOps,

Thanks for agreeing to run inference on Redwood for the initial pilot. Before our kickoff call, we'd like to align on a short prework set so the first implementation session is productive. High-level goals for this engagement: minimize unit cost while meeting your 99th percentile tail-latency target (you mentioned 450ms), pick a safe quantization profile for your accuracy budget, and configure routing + cache behavior for mixed-concurrency traffic.

Could you share the following artifacts by COB Tue?
- 7-day traffic histogram (requests/sec, concurrent active connections) — per endpoint if possible.
- Typical input length distribution (prompt tokens, completion tokens) and 95/99 token lengths.
- A small representative sample of 200-500 requests (stripped of PII) we can replay in the sandbox.
- Accuracy thresholds (BLEU/Exact-match/acceptable %Delta vs your current run).

Suggested prework we'll run on our side:
- Profiling with your sample workload (we'll return a bucketed token-cost breakdown)
- Candidate quant profiles (int8, q4_0, q4_K) with estimated cost/latency tradeoffs
- Baseline routing policy suggestion (latency-first for interactive routes; cost-first for background batch jobs), and cache TTL recommendations for repeated prefixes

Attachments: profile-request-template.csv (small CSV to populate), redwood-quant-matrix.pdf (reference).

Proposed times for a 60-min kickoff (PST): Tue 11/30 10:00, Tue 11/30 13:00, Wed 12/01 09:00. Let me know what works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Primary asks/owners from Redwood:
- Marcus: profiling + quant candidate deck (me)
- Monica: routing & cache policy config + guardrails (cc'd)
- Irene: deployment checklist, sandbox creds + security notes (cc'd)

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachments: profile-request-template.csv (CSV), redwood-quant-matrix.pdf (PDF)

From: Aisha Patel <aisha@brightgrid.ai>

Subject: Re: Runtime economics onboarding sync — batching, cache, quant & routing

Hi Marcus — thanks, this is great.

We can provide the traffic histogram and token-length distribution by end of day Monday (PST). I attached a short CSV export of a 48-hour sample (sanitized) and a link to our S3 bucket with a larger 7-day trace sample. Our initial SLA target is 99th <= 450ms for the interactive route and we're willing to accept up to 2% generation-quality delta vs current model.

Quick notes from EngOps:
- Typical concurrency during peak: 120 concurrent generators across two endpoints (/chat and /summarize).
- Average prompt length: 40 tokens; avg completion: 120 tokens; p99 completion: 700 tokens.
- We have a batch nightly scoring job that can tolerate slower latency but should be routed to cheaper instances.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 11/30 13:00 PST works for Sam and me. We can bring our infra lead if needed.

Link: https://s3.brighgrid.com/brightgrid/onboard-logs/7d-sample.ndjson

Thanks — attaching the 48h-sample.csv now.

—
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightGrid
aisha@brightgrid.ai

Attachments: 48h-sample.csv (CSV)

Subject: Re: Runtime economics onboarding sync — batching, cache, quant & routing

Perfect — thanks Aisha. Calendar invite sent for Tue 11/30 13:00 PST (60m).

For the working session, we'll do the following cadence: 15m alignment + goals, 25m profiler & candidate quant run walkthrough, 15m routing/cache policy recommendations, 5m open actions. Prework checklist (short):
- You: confirm the sandbox API key has read/replay capability for the sample; provide the S3 presigned link or upload to our Drive.
- You: mark which endpoints are interactive vs background (you already flagged /chat and /summarize).
- Us: we'll run the replay, produce a bucketed latency & cost model, and propose 2 quant profiles to validate in canary.

Pre-meeting doc: https://drive.redwood.com/brightgrid/onboard-prework (contains profile-request-template.csv)

Notes on the approach:
- Batching: we'll test micro-batching windows at 20ms/50ms/100ms to study latency tail vs throughput.
- Cache: prefix-based TTL on repeated prefixes — likely short (30s) for chat, multi-minute for summarize if you have high repetition.
- Quant: start with q4_K as a mid-point; if quality delta is <1% we can switch to int8 for nightly batch jobs only.
- Routing: latency-first for interactive routes (pin to low-latency nodes); cost-first for batch (route to quantized nodes and larger batching).

I'll attach the quant matrix we'll walk through and the profile template in the calendar invite. Post-call we'll assign rollout canary steps and success criteria (latency regression tolerance, quality delta threshold).

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
